Description:
Emir Al-Muzaffar al-Ashqar is thirty-five years old and head of the Ashqar branch. His wife is Sul, and they have a daughter, Dilber, aged sixteen, and a younger son, Ibrahim, aged twelve. He is broad-shouldered and grave of face, with a short beard. He wears a deep red silk robe under a black cloak, with a gold-inlaid curved sabre at his belt. The game marks him as a diplomat, and he speaks courteously, often hiding his edge behind a smile.
His youth was overshadowed by the fall of his elders. The XML gives him no father, so any tie to Sunqur al-Ashqar is an inference from the shared name. After Sunqur's revolt collapsed at al-Jassora on 18 June 1280, its followers were arrested, and by inference this clan withdrew to the margins of the court. That experience taught him that against a stronger master the wise course is to bow and endure, not to strike head-on.
Against the rivals of the court he works through sociability and marriage. He hosts banquets, treats guests with courtesy, and draws their relatives into his own circle. He seldom makes an enemy in public, yet he keeps a careful record of every insult and waits for the right moment to repay each one.
His ideal is to restore the Ashqar name to respect in Egypt and Syria, so that his children can stand with dignity. His darkest fear is that after a banquet a trusted aide is exposed as a secret contact of an old enemy, and he, as head of the house, is treated as a conspirator, bringing the whole family to permanent ruin.
Motivations: Restore the Ashqar name to respect in Egypt and Syria, so that the family's young members can stand with dignity.
Build marriage and banquet alliances that bring the rivals' relatives into his circle as lasting friends.
Repay every insult in due time, settling old debts quietly rather than in open quarrels.
Values: Bowing and endurance serve better than open defiance when facing a stronger master.
A courteous word at a feast can win more than a sword, and goodwill must be cultivated patiently.
Every insult must be remembered and every old debt repaid when the moment is ripe, which is the duty of a house head.
Fears: Fears that a trusted aide will be exposed as a secret contact of an old enemy, leaving him branded a conspirator.
Fears that the family will sink into permanent decline, and the Ashqar name will never regain its place at court.
SpeechStyle: Speaks courteously and calmly, often with a smile over a sharper point. He opens with polished compliments, then presses his case with a quiet question. When the revolt or his elders come up, he turns measured and avoids direct blame.
